lessons.sub: loops inside loops; repetition counting; daily patterns
teaching: A nested loop means putting a smaller loop inside a bigger loop.
Think of clapping twice during each of your three daily exercise rounds.
Try acting out clapping two times for every jump you make.
Always count the inner steps carefully before repeating the outer loop.
lessons.explainAr: التكرار المتداخل يعني وضع تكرار صغير جوه تكرار كبير عشان ننظم وقتنا صح. ده بيخلينا نعمل حاجات كتيرة ومنظمة من غير ما نتعب.
lessons.exampleEn: Doing two stretches inside each of three morning exercises.
lessons.exampleAr: عمل تمارين إطالة مرتين جوه كل تمرين من الثلاث تمارين الصباحية.
lessons.practiceEn: Clap your hands twice for every single step you take forward.
lessons.practiceAr: صفق بيديك مرتين مع كل خطوة بتاخدها لقدام.
steps: A nested loop is when you put one loop inside another loop to repeat things efficiently.
For example, you clap your hands twice during every single jump you do.
How it works: the inner loop finishes completely before the outer loop moves to the next turn.
Another example is brushing each of your two rows of teeth with three brush strokes.
Rule of thumb: count the inner actions carefully so you do not mix up your rounds.
Real-life use: factory machines packaging boxes inside a larger shipping container.
lessons.example: Imagine marching in place: you blink your eyes three times during every single step you take forward.
lessons.mistake: Forgetting to reset the inner loop counter when the outer loop moves to the next step.
lessons.recap: Nested loops let us repeat small tasks inside larger repeating routines easily. They save time and keep our steps organized.

q.t: What is a nested loop?
q.why: It is a loop placed inside a bigger loop.

q.t: Which loop finishes first?
q.why: The inner loop runs completely for every single step of the outer loop.

q.t: Why do we use nested loops?
q.why: They help us organize and repeat tasks without writing extra instructions.

act.title: Nested Dance Steps
act.goal: Put the nested routine steps in the correct order.
items: Start the outer loop for 2 big turns
Begin the inner loop for 3 claps
Finish the big turn and repeat
act.success: Your robot performed the awesome nested dance routine perfectly!

lessons.sub: multiple conditions; if-else-if logic; decision making
teaching: Complex conditions let us check more than one rule before deciding.
If it is sunny wear a hat, else if it is rainy take an umbrella.
Try sorting clothes based on the weather outside your window.
Check conditions one by one from top to bottom so nothing overlaps.
lessons.explainAr: الخيارات الشرطية المعقدة بتخلينا نختار بين حاجات كتير بناءً على أكتر من شرط. ده بيساعدنا ناخد القرار الصح في أي موقف.
lessons.exampleEn: Choosing a jacket based on whether it is cold, rainy, or hot outside.
lessons.exampleAr: اختيار الجاكيت بناءً على حالة الطقس لو كان برد، ممطر، أو حار.
lessons.practiceEn: Stand up if the card is red, sit down if blue, and turn around if green.
lessons.practiceAr: اقف لو الكارت أحمر، اقعد لو أزرق، ولف حوالين نفسك لو أخضر.
steps: Complex conditions let us check multiple rules to make smart choices.
For example, if it is raining take an umbrella, else if it is sunny wear sunglasses.
How it works: we test conditions one by one until we find the matching rule.
Another example is choosing your snack based on hunger level and mealtime.
Rule of thumb: always check the most specific rule first.
Real-life use: traffic lights changing based on car counts and pedestrian buttons.
lessons.example: If the light is green walk, if yellow wait, if red stop completely.
lessons.mistake: Putting a general rule at the top so specific rules never get checked.
lessons.recap: Complex conditions handle multiple choices by testing rules one by one. They help us make precise decisions in changing situations.

q.t: When do we use complex conditions?
o: When we have only one choice
When we have multiple rules to check
q.why: They help us test more than one rule before deciding.

q.t: In what order are conditions checked?
q.why: We check conditions sequentially from the first rule down.

q.t: What happens if the first condition is true?
o: We skip the rest and do that action
We check all other rules anyway
q.why: Once a matching rule is found, its action is executed immediately.

act.title: Weather Outfit Sorting
act.goal: Sort the actions into the correct weather condition.
act.success: You dressed up correctly for the weather using smart conditions!

lessons.sub: rows and columns; grid maps; exact positions
teaching: A grid coordinate system uses rows and columns to find exact spots.
Think of finding row 2 and column 3 on a game board.
Try placing a toy at position A1 on a drawn floor grid.
Always read the horizontal column first, then the vertical row.
lessons.explainAr: نظام الإحداثيات بيساعدنا نعرف مكان أي حاجة بدقة باستخدام الصفوف والأعمدة. ده عامل زي الخريطة اللي ليها خطوط مربعة واضحة.
lessons.exampleEn: Finding the treasure located at column 2, row 3 on the map.
lessons.exampleAr: إيجاد الكنز الموجود في العمود الثاني والصف الثالث على الخريطة.
lessons.practiceEn: Point to column 1 and row 2 on your classroom tile floor.
lessons.practiceAr: شاور على العمود الأول والصف الثاني في بلاط الفصل.
steps: Grid coordinate systems help us pinpoint exact locations using rows and columns.
For example, locating your desk at column 3 and row 2 in the classroom.
How it works: we combine a letter or number for the column with one for the row.
Another example is playing chess where pieces move to squares like E4.
Rule of thumb: always check the horizontal position before the vertical position.
Real-life use: GPS maps finding your exact location on planet Earth.
lessons.example: Placing a game token at column 4, row 1 on a checkerboard.
lessons.mistake: Swapping the row and column numbers and looking at the wrong spot.
lessons.recap: Grids use rows and columns to give every single square a unique address. This makes navigation precise and foolproof.

q.t: What does a grid coordinate use?
q.why: It uses rows and columns to map exact locations.

q.t: What should you check first on a standard grid?
q.why: We check the horizontal column before the vertical row.

q.t: Why are coordinates useful?
o: To find exact spots without getting lost
q.why: They give every position a unique address so we never get lost.

act.title: Grid Treasure Match
act.goal: Match each map item to its correct grid coordinate.
act.success: All map items were located accurately on the coordinate grid!

lessons.sub: optimal routes; avoiding obstacles; shortest path
teaching: Pathfinding is figuring out the best route from start to finish.
Think of walking around a desk instead of bumping into it.
Try drawing a path on paper that avoids three eraser obstacles.
Always look for the shortest, safest route without dead ends.
lessons.explainAr: البحث عن المسار بيساعدنا نلاقي أحسن وأسرع طريق من نقطة البداية للنهاية من غير ما نخبط في عوائق. ده بيخلي حركتنا ذكية ومنظمة.
lessons.exampleEn: Walking around a chair to reach the door without bumping into it.
lessons.exampleAr: المشي من حوالين الكرسي عشان توصل الباب من غير ما تخبط فيه.
lessons.practiceEn: Guide your finger around a book maze from top to bottom.
lessons.practiceAr: وجه صباعك حوالين متاهة الكتاب من البداية للنهاية من غير عوائق.
steps: Pathfinding is the process of finding the best route from a start point to a goal.
For example, walking around a school bag in the hallway to reach the whiteboard.
How it works: we look ahead, spot obstacles, and plan steps around them.
Another example is finding the fastest corridor during a fire drill.
Rule of thumb: the shortest path with zero obstacles is always the best choice.
Real-life use: delivery robots navigating busy hospital hallways.
lessons.example: Stepping around a puddle on the playground to keep your shoes dry.
lessons.mistake: Choosing a straight line that crashes right into an obstacle.
lessons.recap: Advanced pathfinding helps us navigate around obstacles smoothly. It ensures we reach our destinations safely and efficiently.

q.t: What is pathfinding?
o: Finding the best route from start to finish
q.why: It is planning the best route while avoiding obstacles.

q.t: What should you do when you see an obstacle?
o: Stop and plan a way around it
q.why: We plan steps around obstacles to stay safe.

q.t: Which path is usually the best?
o: The longest one with many traps
The shortest safe path with no obstacles
q.why: The shortest safe path saves time and avoids hazards.

act.title: Safe Route Choice
act.goal: Predict which path safely reaches the toy.
options: Turn right, 1 step forward, turn left
Keep walking straight into the obstacle
Turn around and go back to start
act.why: Turning right and stepping around the obstacle avoids the crash.
act.success: Your robot successfully bypassed the obstacle and reached the toy!

lessons.sub: repeating shapes; sequence prediction; logic patterns
teaching: Pattern recognition means finding repeating rules in a sequence.
Think of a row of shapes: circle, square, circle, square.
Try guessing what shape comes next after red, blue, red, blue.
Always look at the first few items to find the repeating core.
lessons.explainAr: التعرف على الأنماط بيخلينا نكتشف الحاجات اللي بتتكرر بنظام معين. ده بيساعدنا نتوقع الخطوة اللي جايّة بكل سهولة.
lessons.exampleEn: Predicting that a star comes next after moon, star, moon, star.
lessons.exampleAr: توقع أن النجمة هي اللي هتجيء بعد قمر، نجمة، قمر، نجمة.
lessons.practiceEn: Clap, stomp, clap, stomp — what comes next?
lessons.practiceAr: صفقة، خبطة رجل، صفقة، خبطة رجل — إيه اللي جاي بعد كده؟
steps: Pattern recognition is finding the repeating rule inside any sequence.
For example, noticing red, blue, red, blue in a row of beads.
How it works: we study the core pattern and extend it forward.
Another example is predicting morning, afternoon, night, morning.
Rule of thumb: find the smallest repeating chunk first.
Real-life use: predicting weather seasons or musical beats in a song.
lessons.example: Completing the sequence: up, down, up, down, up.
lessons.mistake: Changing the pattern halfway through without noticing the rule.
lessons.recap: Pattern recognition helps us predict what comes next in any sequence. It is a powerful tool for logical thinking.

q.t: What is a pattern?
o: A rule that repeats in order
q.why: A pattern is a sequence that repeats following a specific rule.

q.t: What comes after: circle, triangle, circle, triangle?
q.why: The pattern alternates between circle and triangle, so circle is next.

q.t: Why do we find patterns?
q.why: Patterns help us predict future steps accurately.

act.title: Fix the Broken Pattern
act.goal: Find the wrong item in the repeating pattern sequence.
act.success: The pattern sequence is now fixed and repeats correctly!

lessons.sub: true and false; yes or no; binary choices
teaching: Boolean logic is about answers that are strictly True or False.
Think of the statement: 'The sky is blue today' — it is True.
Try deciding if 'Cats can fly' is True or False.
Always remember a statement cannot be both True and False at once.
lessons.explainAr: المنطق البولياني بيتعامل مع إجابات صح أو خطأ بس (True أو False). ده بيساعد الكمبيوتر ياخد قرارات واضحة من غير تردد.
lessons.exampleEn: The statement 'Water is wet' evaluates to True.
lessons.exampleAr: جملة 'الماء مبلل' تقييمها صحيح (True).
lessons.practiceEn: Clap if 'Fish live in water' is True.
lessons.practiceAr: صفق لو جملة 'السمك يعيش في الماء' صحيحة.
steps: Boolean logic deals with statements that are either True or False.
For example, 'Dogs have four legs' is True.
How it works: every question has only two possible truth values.
Another example is '10 is smaller than 5' which is False.
Rule of thumb: a statement must be clearly True or clearly False.
Real-life use: light switches being either ON (True) or OFF (False).
lessons.example: Deciding if 'Fire is hot' is True.
lessons.mistake: Trying to make a maybe answer instead of choosing True or False.
lessons.recap: Boolean logic uses True and False to make clear binary decisions. It forms the foundation of all computer processing.

q.t: What are the two values in Boolean logic?
q.why: Boolean logic only uses True and False.

q.t: Is 'The sun is hot' True or False?
q.why: The sun is indeed hot, so it is True.

q.t: Can a Boolean statement be both True and False?
q.why: A statement must be one or the other, never both.

act.title: True or False Sorting
act.goal: Sort the statements into True and False buckets.
act.success: All statements were correctly sorted into True and False!

lessons.sub: logical operators; combining conditions; and/or rules
teaching: We can combine conditions using AND and OR to make stronger rules.
AND means both rules must be true; OR means at least one must be true.
Try checking if you have a pencil AND an eraser.
Always test each part of the combined rule carefully.
lessons.explainAr: بنقدر نجمع الشروط باستخدام أداتين: AND (ولازم الاتنين يتحققوا) و OR (يكفي شرط واحد يتحقق). ده بيدينا قوة أكبر في اتخاذ القرار.
lessons.exampleEn: Going outside requires (Sun is shining OR No rain).
lessons.exampleAr: الخروج للخارج يتطلب (الشمس ساطعة أو لا يوجد مطر).
lessons.practiceEn: Jump if you are wearing red AND smiling.
lessons.practiceAr: انط لو لابس أحمر وبتبتسم في نفس الوقت.
steps: We combine conditions using logical operators like AND and OR.
For example, to play outside you need (Sun is out AND It is daytime).
How it works: AND requires all conditions to be true, while OR needs just one.
Another example: you can eat fruit OR vegetables for a healthy snack.
Rule of thumb: check AND rules strictly, but OR rules flexibly.
Real-life use: password security requiring letters AND numbers.
lessons.example: To win the prize you need a ticket AND a lucky number.
lessons.mistake: Treating AND like OR and thinking only one rule is enough.
lessons.recap: AND and OR help us build powerful combined conditions. They make our logical tests much more flexible.

q.t: What does AND mean in conditions?
o: Only one rule must be true
All connected rules must be true
q.why: AND requires every condition connected by it to be true.

q.t: What does OR mean in conditions?
o: At least one rule must be true
q.why: OR is satisfied if at least one of the conditions is true.

q.t: If rule A is true and rule B is false, does (A AND B) pass?
q.why: AND requires both to be true; since B is false, it fails.

act.title: AND vs OR Game
act.goal: Predict if the combined condition passes.
options: No, because AND needs both to be true
act.why: AND requires both items to be true, so it fails here.
act.success: You mastered combined logical conditions successfully!

lessons.sub: remembering states; tracking values; state machines
teaching: State means remembering the current condition of something over time.
Think of a light switch remembering whether it is currently ON or OFF.
Try holding up one finger to show your lamp is ON, zero for OFF.
Always update your memory state whenever an action changes it.
lessons.explainAr: الحالة بتعني إننا نفتكر وضع حاجة معينة دلوقتي هل هو شغال ولا طافي. ده عامل زي ذاكرة المخ اللي بتفتكر إحنا عملنا إيه.
lessons.exampleEn: The door remembering whether it is locked or unlocked.
lessons.exampleAr: الباب يتذكر ما إذا كان مقفول أو مفتوح.
lessons.practiceEn: Turn your palm up for 'Active' state, down for 'Resting'.
lessons.practiceAr: قلب إيدك لفوق لحالة 'نشط' ولتحت لحالة 'مستريح'.
steps: State refers to storing the current condition of an object in memory.
For example, a television remembering whether it is muted or has sound.
How it works: we keep track of the status and update it when things change.
Another example is a game scoreboard remembering your points.
Rule of thumb: always keep your memory updated so you know the current state.
Real-life use: smart thermostats remembering your preferred room temperature.
lessons.example: A traffic light remembering it was green, then switching to red.
lessons.mistake: Forgetting to update the state variable when an action happens.
lessons.recap: State and memory let programs remember information over time. This makes interactive logic possible.

q.t: What is 'state' in logic?
q.why: State is the stored condition of an object at any moment.

q.t: Why do we need memory in programs?
o: To remember current values like scores and light states
q.why: Memory lets us keep track of important data over time.

q.t: What happens when a light switch is flipped from ON to OFF?
q.why: Fليpping the switch updates its state in memory.

act.title: State and Action Match
act.goal: Match each device to its changing state.
act.success: All device states were tracked and matched correctly!

lessons.sub: making steps shorter; efficiency; code optimization
teaching: Optimizing means finding a shorter, smarter way to do the same task.
Think of taking 3 steps right instead of 1 step right three separate times.
Try combining four walking steps into one single 'walk 4 steps' card.
Always look for repeated actions you can simplify.
lessons.explainAr: التحسين معناه إنا نعمل الشغل بطريقة أسرع وأقصر من غير ما نغير النتيجة. ده بيخلي خطواتنا أرتب وأسهل في التنفيذ.
lessons.exampleEn: Using a loop card instead of writing the same instruction five times.
lessons.exampleAr: استخدام كارت تكرار بدل ما نكتب نفس الأمر خمس مرات.
lessons.practiceEn: Combine three claps into one clap-three-times command.
lessons.practiceAr: اجمع ثلاث صفقات في أمر واحد 'صفق ثلاث مرات'.
steps: Optimization is about making instructions shorter and more efficient.
For example, replacing 4 forward steps with a single 'repeat 4 times' rule.
How it works: we spot repeated or clumsy steps and streamline them.
Another example is packing your bag the night before to save morning time.
Rule of thumb: fewer instructions mean fewer chances for bugs.
Real-life use: video game programmers making their code run faster.
lessons.example: Writing 'walk 5 steps' instead of 'walk, walk, walk, walk, walk'.
lessons.mistake: Making instructions too short and missing necessary safety steps.
lessons.recap: Optimizing sequences makes our instructions cleaner and faster. Efficiency is a key skill in logical thinking.

q.t: What is optimization?
o: Finding a smarter, shorter way to do tasks
q.why: Optimization means improving efficiency and reducing clutter.

q.t: Why do we optimize step sequences?
o: To save time and avoid repetitive writing
q.why: Shorter instructions save time and prevent errors.

q.t: What is shorter: writing walk 5 times or using a loop?
q.why: A loop is much shorter and more efficient.

act.title: Optimize the Routine
act.goal: Order the steps to transform long instructions into an optimized loop.
items: Notice the step is repeated 5 times
act.success: The instruction sequence is now fully optimized and clean!

lessons.sub: integrating loops; conditions; pathfinding; final project
teaching: Let's combine everything we learned into one big robot maze adventure.
Use grids, coordinates, loops, and conditions to guide your robot home.
Try acting out the final path from start to finish without any bugs.
Always review your full algorithm step by step before finishing.
lessons.explainAr: يلا نجمع كل اللي تعلمناه في مشروع ممتع واحد للمتاهة الذكية. هنستخدم التكرارات، الشروط، والإحداثيات عشان نوصل الروبوت لهدفه.
lessons.exampleEn: Guiding your robot through a grid maze using loops and conditions.
lessons.exampleAr: توجيه الروبوت خلال متاهة شبكية باستخدام التكرارات والشروط.
lessons.practiceEn: Execute your final master algorithm from start to finish!
lessons.practiceAr: نفذ خوارزميتك الرئيسية النهلئية من البداية للنهاية!
steps: The term project brings together all our algorithmic skills into one challenge.
For example, guiding a robot across a grid using loops, conditions, and coordinates.
How it works: we plan the path, check for obstacles, and use loops for efficiency.
Another example is building a board game where players navigate using rules.
Rule of thumb: test each part of your project before putting it all together.
Real-life use: aerospace engineers assembling all parts of a space rocket.
lessons.example: Successfully navigating the maze from column 1 to the treasure at column 3.
lessons.mistake: Rوشing through the final check and missing a small bug in the path.
lessons.recap: Our term project combined loops, conditions, and grid logic into a complete solution. You are now a true algorithmic thinker!

q.t: What skills do we combine in the term project?
q.why: We integrate all the major concepts learned throughout the term.

q.t: Why should you test your final project?
o: To make sure there are no bugs
q.why: Testing ensures every step works correctly before finishing.

q.t: What is the goal of the smart robot maze?
o: To reach the goal safely using smart logic
q.why: The goal is successful navigation using all our algorithmic tools.

act.title: Smart Robot Master Plan
act.goal: Put the term project steps in the correct execution order.
items: Apply the pathfinding route around obstacles
Use a loop for repeated walking steps
Reach the final treasure goal successfully
act.success: Your smart robot completed the final maze project brilliantly!

lessons.sub: backgrounds; scenes; world building; scratchjr
teaching: Backgrounds change where your story takes place.
Pick a castle or space scene from the library.
Tap the landscape icon at the top of your screen.
Always match your background to your story theme.
lessons.explainAr: الخلفيات بتغير مكان القصة وتخليها شكلها جميل. تقدر تختار خلفية فضاء أو حديقة من زر المناظر الطبيعية فوق.
lessons.exampleEn: Choosing a jungle background makes the monkey sprite feel right at home.
lessons.exampleAr: اختيار خلفية غابة بيخلي شخصية القرد في مكانها الطبيعي.
lessons.practiceEn: Add a new background to your project right now.
lessons.practiceAr: ضيف خلفية جديدة لمشروعك دلوقتي.
steps: Backgrounds set the stage and visual mood for your entire ScratchJr story scene, letting characters move through exciting new locations instead of a plain white screen.
For example, you can tap the landscape icon at the top right to select a sunny beach backdrop for your crab character.
It works by replacing the empty stage with a colourful image chosen from the built-in ScratchJr library or one you draw yourself using the paint tool.
Another great example is switching from a daytime city to a starry night sky when your story character goes to sleep.
Rule of thumb: Always pick your background first before placing sprites so you know where everything belongs in your animated world.
Real-life use: Just like theatre sets change between acts in a school play, digital backgrounds show the audience where the story action is happening.
lessons.example: If your cat is exploring outer space, adding the moon backdrop instantly makes the adventure feel real and exciting for anyone watching your project.
lessons.mistake: Adding sprites before choosing a background and then having to rearrange all their starting positions. Fix it by picking your background scene first.
lessons.recap: Backgrounds transform your project setting. They create visual context for your storytelling adventures.

q.t: Where do you tap to add a new background in ScratchJr?
o: The landscape icon at the top
q.why: The landscape icon opens the background selection menu.

q.t: Why are backgrounds important in a story?
o: They make the project run faster
They show where the story takes place
q.why: Backgrounds give context to the location of the action.

q.t: When is the best time to choose your background?
q.why: Choosing it first helps you place your sprites correctly.

act.title: Scene Change
act.goal: Predict what happens when you tap the landscape icon
act.code: Tap the landscape icon at the top of the ScratchJr screen.
options: It opens the background library to pick a new scene
act.success: The background library opens and your stage transforms into a brand new world!

lessons.sub: paint editor; drawing; sprites; scratchjr
teaching: You can draw your own unique characters in ScratchJr.
Tap the plus sign and choose the paintbrush tool.
Use shapes and colours to create a friendly monster.
Always give your custom sprite a fun, memorable name.
lessons.explainAr: تقدر ترسم شخصيتك الخاصة بنفسك باستخدام فرشاه الرسم. اضغط على علامة الزائد واختار أداة الرسم عشان تعمل وحش لطيف.
lessons.exampleEn: Drawing a purple alien lets you star a totally original hero in your story.
lessons.exampleAr: رسم كائن فضائي بنفسجي بيخليك تعمل بطل أصلي تماماً في قصتك.
lessons.practiceEn: Draw a custom smiley face sprite using the paint editor.
lessons.practiceAr: ارسم شخصية وجه مبتسم مخصصة باستخدام محرّر الرسم.
steps: Designing custom characters lets you bring your own imagination to life instead of relying only on the default ScratchJr sprite library.
For example, you can tap the plus sign with a paintbrush to open the drawing editor and sketch a friendly purple alien.
It works by using digital painting tools like shapes, lines, and paint buckets to colour your creation pixel by pixel right on screen.
Another example is drawing a magical flying pizza slice to act as the main hero of your funny food adventure story.
Rule of thumb: Keep your custom drawings simple with bold outlines so they look clear even when scaled smaller on the stage.
Real-life use: Concept artists and character designers draw unique heroes for animated movies and video games every single day.
lessons.example: By tapping the paint tool and using the circle shape filled with yellow, you can instantly create your very own bouncing sun character.
lessons.mistake: Drawing details that are too tiny and messy which disappear when the sprite shrinks. Fix it by using bold, clean shapes.
lessons.recap: Custom characters make your projects totally unique. The paint editor gives you creative freedom.

q.t: What tool opens the drawing editor for custom sprites?
q.why: The paintbrush lets you draw and paint custom characters.

q.t: Why should you keep custom drawings simple?
o: So they stay clear when small
q.why: Simple shapes and bold outlines remain visible on stage.

q.t: How do you start creating a brand new sprite?
o: Tap the plus sign on the left side
q.why: The plus sign adds a new sprite to your project.

act.title: Paint a Sprite
act.goal: Put the custom sprite creation steps in correct order
items: Tap the plus sign on the left side of the screen
Select the paintbrush icon to open the paint editor
Draw your custom character using shapes and colours
Tap the checkmark to save your new sprite
act.success: Your custom character appears proudly on the stage ready for action!

lessons.sub: repeat forever; endless loops; animation; scratchjr
teaching: Repeat forever loops keep actions running without stopping.
Wrap blocks inside the red loop with the arrow circle.
A fish can swim back and forth across the ocean forever.
Always add a stop block if you need to break the loop.
lessons.explainAr: حلقات التكرار المستمر بتخلي الحركات شغالة علطول من غير ما تقف. حط الأجو جوه المربع الأحمر عشان السمكة تعوم بلا توقف.
lessons.exampleEn: A spinning star keeps rotating endlessly to show it is magical.
lessons.exampleAr: النجمة بتفضل تلف بلا نهاية عشان توضح إنها سحرية.
lessons.practiceEn: Make a character bounce up and down forever using a loop.
lessons.practiceAr: خلی شخصية تنط لفوق وتحت للأبد باستخدام حلقة تكرار.
steps: Repeat forever loops are special control blocks that run the blocks placed inside them endlessly until the user presses the stop sign.
For example, you can snap a move-right and move-left block inside a red forever loop to make a crab patrol the beach constantly.
It works by looping the inner sequence of commands back to the beginning the exact moment the final inner block finishes executing.
Another example is making a twinkling star sprite pulse in size over and over without any manual intervention from the player.
Rule of thumb: Use forever loops for background animations like clouds drifting or water flowing, but avoid them for interactive puzzles.
Real-life use: Digital clocks and animated loading spinners on websites use endless loops to keep working smoothly without pausing.
lessons.example: Placing a turn-right block inside a red repeat-forever block turns your wheel sprite into a spinning fan that never stops.
lessons.mistake: Forgetting that forever loops never end on their own, meaning your sprite will keep going until you hit stop. Fix it by testing with the stop sign handy.
lessons.recap: Endless loops keep background action alive. They automate continuous motion easily.

q.t: What colour is the repeat forever loop block in ScratchJr?

q.t: When does a repeat-forever loop stop running?

q.why: Pressing the red stop sign halts all active scripts.

q.t: What is a good use for a forever loop?
o: A character walking back and forth endlessly
q.why: Endless walking is great for background atmosphere.

lessons.sub: speed blocks; fast; slow; scratchjr
teaching: Speed blocks make your sprites move fast or slow.

Use the slow speed block for a sneaky turtle.

lessons.explainAr: أبلكيشن سكراتش جونيور بيخليك تغير سرعة الشخصيات بسرعة أو ببطء. استخدم بلوك السرعة السريعة لعربية سباق.
lessons.exampleEn: A cheetah uses fast speed while a snail uses slow speed.
lessons.exampleAr: الفهد بيستخدم سرعة عالية بينما القوقعة بتمشي ببطء شديد.
lessons.practiceEn: Make a rocket zoom across the screen using the fast speed block.
lessons.practiceAr: خلی صاروخ يطير بسرعة عبر الشاشة باستخدام بلوك السرعة.
steps: Speed blocks change how fast your sprite executes motion commands like walking, jumping, or gliding across the stage.
For example, you can attach a fast speed block to make a race car zoom past in a flash.
It works by multiplying the default frame rate of movement steps, making animations zip by or crawl leisurely.
Another example is setting a snail sprite to slow speed so it creeps across the garden path realistically.
Rule of thumb: Set your speed block right at the start of your script before any motion blocks happen.
Real-life use: Video game developers adjust character speeds to make running feel powerful and sneaking feel tense.
lessons.example: Snapping a super-fast speed block onto a lightning bolt sprite makes it strike instantly when the green flag is tapped.
lessons.mistake: Placing the speed block after the motion blocks instead of before. Fix it by putting the speed modifier first in your stack.
lessons.recap: Speed blocks control animation pacing. Fast and slow speeds add drama to scenes.

q.t: Where should you place the speed block in your script?
o: At the very end of the script
q.why: Speed must be set before movement begins.

q.t: Which speed block is best for a crawling caterpillar?
q.why: Slow speed matches crawling animals.

q.t: What do speed blocks change?
q.why: They alter the pacing of sprite motions.

lessons.sub: wait blocks; pauses; timing; scratchjr
teaching: Wait blocks pause your code for a few moments.
Use a wait block to let another character speak first.
Set the number of seconds to control the pause length.
Good timing makes conversations feel natural in stories.
lessons.explainAr: بلوك الانتظار بيوقف الكود لفترة قصيرة عشان يخلي شخصية تخلص كلام قبل ما التانية تبدأ. ظبط عدد الثواني عشان القصة تكون طبيعية.
lessons.exampleEn: The cat waits two seconds for the dog to finish barking.
lessons.exampleAr: القطة بتستنى ثانيتين لحد ما الكلب يخلص نباح.
lessons.practiceEn: Add a one-second wait between two speech bubbles.
lessons.practiceAr: ضيف انتظار ثانية واحدة بين فقاعتين كلام.
steps: Wait blocks introduce a deliberate pause in your script, letting you control the exact timing and rhythm of story events.
For example, you can make a cat say hello, wait two seconds, and then wave goodbye.
It works by holding the script execution for a specified number of frames before passing to the next block in the stack.
Another example is staging a magical appearance where a fairy waits one second before popping onto the screen.
Rule of thumb: Use wait blocks to give the audience time to read speech bubbles before characters move again.
Real-life use: Movie directors use dramatic pauses in dialogue to build suspense and make conversations feel realistic.
lessons.example: Putting a wait-3-seconds block between two jump commands makes your dancer pause dramatically mid-routine.
lessons.mistake: Setting the wait time too long and making the user think the program froze. Fix it by keeping waits between 1 to 3 seconds.
lessons.recap: Wait blocks manage timing and pacing. They give viewers time to read and react.

q.t: What does a wait block do in a script?
o: Pauses code execution for a set time
q.why: Wait blocks pause scripts for specified seconds.

q.t: Why would you use a wait block after a speech bubble?
o: To give viewers time to read the text
To make the sprite walk faster
q.why: Audiences need time to read dialogue before action resumes.

q.t: Which block colour category includes the wait block?
q.why: Control and timing blocks are orange/yellow in ScratchJr.

lessons.sub: pages; multi-page stories; navigation; scratchjr
teaching: Longer stories need more than one page to grow.
Tap the plus page button on the right to add page 2.
Use the goto page block to jump from page 1 to page 2.
Every page can have its own unique characters and background.
lessons.explainAr: القصص الطويلة محتاجة أكتر من صفحة. اضغط على زر الصفحة الزيادة ع اليمين، واستخدم بلوك الانتقال لفتح الصفحة التانية.
lessons.exampleEn: Page 1 is daytime in the park, and page 2 is nighttime in space.
lessons.exampleAr: الصفحة الأولى نهار في الحديقة، والصفحة التانية ليل في الفضاء.
lessons.practiceEn: Create page 2 and link your first page to it.
lessons.practiceAr: اعمل الصفحة التانية وربطها بصفحتك الأولى.
steps: Multi-page projects let you expand your creative storytelling beyond a single screen by linking multiple independent stages together.
For example, your character can explore a sunny forest on Page 1 and then travel inside a mysterious cave on Page 2.
It works by using the orange page-turn block at the end of a script to switch the entire stage view to a new workspace.
Another example is creating a multi-level game where beating level 1 automatically jumps the player to the winning celebration page.
Rule of thumb: Plan what happens on each page on paper first so your story flows smoothly from beginning to end.
Real-life use: Storybook apps and comic books use separate pages to guide readers through different chapters of an adventure.
lessons.example: Adding the go-to-page-2 block when the rocket reaches the top of Page 1 transports your astronaut straight to the moon scene.
lessons.mistake: Forgetting to create Page 2 before trying to use the jump block. Fix it by tapping the add-page button first.
lessons.recap: Pages let you tell epic multi-part stories. Go-to blocks seamlessly connect your scenes.

q.t: How do you add a new page in a ScratchJr project?
o: Tap the plus page button on the right side
q.why: The page list on the right has an add-page button.

q.t: What block sends your sprite to another page?
q.why: The page-turn block navigates to specific project pages.

q.t: Why are multiple pages useful for stories?
o: They let you tell longer adventures with new scenes
q.why: Multiple pages allow scene changes and chapter progression.

lessons.sub: messages; broadcasts; communication; scratchjr
teaching: Mailbox messages let sprites talk and trigger actions together.
Sprite A sends a red mailbox message when it finishes talking.
Sprite B starts its script when it receives the red message.
Matching message colours ensures the right characters cooperate.
lessons.explainAr: رسائل صندوق البريد بتخلي الشخصيات تتكلم وتشتغل مع بعض. الشخصية الأولى تبعت رسالة حمراء، والشخصية التانية تبدأ لما تستلمها.
lessons.exampleEn: The cat sends a message, and the dog starts dancing upon receiving it.
lessons.exampleAr: القطة بتعت والرسالة، والكلب بيبدأ يرقص أول ما يستلمها.
lessons.practiceEn: Send a green message from a wizard to make a potion sparkle.
lessons.practiceAr: ابعث رسالة خضراء من الساحر عشان تخلي الجرعة تتلألأ.
steps: Message triggers allow different sprites on the stage to communicate and coordinate their actions using colour-coded broadcast signals.
For example, a magician sprite can send a red mail message that tells a rabbit sprite to pop out of a hat.
It works by having one sprite output a send-message block and another sprite use the matching colour message-received start trigger.
Another example is a starter whistle in a sports game where the referee broadcasts a message for runners to dash forward.
Rule of thumb: Keep track of your message colours so different events in your story do not accidentally trigger each other.
Real-life use: Walkie-talkies and emergency broadcast systems send signals across distances to coordinate teamwork instantly.
lessons.example: When the pirate taps the treasure chest, it sends a yellow message making the parrot squawk and fly away.
lessons.mistake: Using different message colours for the sender and receiver, causing the second sprite to never react. Fix it by matching the colours.
lessons.recap: Messages connect different sprites into a team. Broadcast signals coordinate interactive stories.

q.t: What is the purpose of message blocks in ScratchJr?
o: To let sprites communicate and trigger each other's code
q.why: Messages allow sprites to broadcast signals to one another.

q.t: How does the receiving sprite know when to start?
o: By using the matching colour message start trigger
q.why: The receive-message hat block starts when that colour is broadcast.

q.t: What happens if message colours do not match?
o: The second sprite will not react to the signal
q.why: Senders and receivers must use identical colours to communicate.

lessons.sub: sound; recording; microphone; scratchjr
teaching: Sound blocks bring your digital story to life with audio.
Use the pop sound block for fun cartoon actions.
Tap the microphone icon to record your own custom voice.
Personal voice lines make animated storytelling extra special.

lessons.exampleEn: Recording your own roar makes your dinosaur sprite sound super scary.
lessons.exampleAr: تسجيل زئير بصوتك بيخلي شخصية الديناصور مخيفة جداً.

steps: Sound blocks and audio recordings let you add personality, dialogue, and fun sound effects to your animated characters.

Rule of thumb: Keep recorded voice clips short and clear so they match the exact moment of the animation.
Real-life use: Voice actors spend hours recording dialogue lines for cartoon characters and video game heroes.
lessons.example: Attaching the record-voice block lets your drawing of a puppy bark whenever someone taps it.
lessons.mistake: Speaking too quietly into the tablet microphone during recording. Fix it by speaking clearly and close to the device.
lessons.recap: Audio enriches digital storytelling. Custom voice recordings make projects deeply personal.

lessons.sub: storyboard; planning; design; scratchjr
teaching: A storyboard is a paper plan before you start coding.
Draw your beginning, middle, and end on three paper boxes.
Plan which characters speak and where they walk.
Planning ahead saves time and makes epic stories.

lessons.exampleEn: Sketching a cat finding a fish on paper keeps your project organized.
lessons.exampleAr: رسم قطة بتلاقي سمكة على الورق بيخلي مشروعك منظم.
lessons.practiceEn: Draw a 3-part storyboard for a new animal adventure.
lessons.practiceAr: ارسم قصة من 3 خطوات لمغامرة حيوان جديدة.
steps: A storyboard is a visual planning tool where you sketch your story on paper before touching a single block of code.
For example, you draw three boxes showing a dog running in box 1, finding a bone in box 2, and celebrating in box 3.
It works by mapping out characters, backgrounds, and plot twists sequentially so you have a clear roadmap for your project.
Another example is noting down which page numbers and sound effects belong to each scene during planning.
Rule of thumb: Always outline your beginning, middle, and end on paper before opening the ScratchJr app.
Real-life use: Filmmakers and animators draw thousands of storyboard sketches to plan every scene of a blockbuster movie.
lessons.example: Sketching your story scenes on sticky notes helps you rearrange the plot order easily before building it in ScratchJr.
lessons.mistake: Jumping straight into coding without any plan and getting confused about what happens next. Fix it by sketching a quick 3-box storyboard first.
lessons.recap: Storyboards make complex projects easy. Planning on paper leads to better coding.

lessons.exampleEn: A multi-page space rescue mission featuring custom aliens, sounds, and loops.
lessons.exampleAr: مهمة إنقاذ فضائية من صفحات متعددة فيها كائنات مخصصة وأصوات وحلقات تكرار.
lessons.practiceEn: Build a complete two-page story with a custom character and sound.
lessons.practiceAr: ابني قصة كاملة من صفحتين بشخصية مخصصة وصوت.
steps: The grand finale project is your chance to combine every skill you mastered this term into one magnificent animated story.

lessons.sub: jump count; variables; mid-air jump; reset on touch
teaching: Learn how characters can jump again while already in the air.
Use a counter variable to track how many jumps are left.
Set the jump counter to two when touching the ground.
Always reset your air jumps safely whenever you land.
lessons.explainAr: هتعلم إزاي نخلي الشخصية تنط تاني وهي في الهواء. بنستخدم متغير عشان نعد النطّات ونصفرها لما نلمس الأرض.
lessons.exampleEn: When space is pressed and air jumps are greater than zero, change y and reduce the jump count.
lessons.exampleAr: لما ندوس مسافة والنطّات المتبقية أكبر من صفر، نغير ص ونقلل العداد واحد.
lessons.practiceEn: Add a double jump to your platformer cat.
lessons.practiceAr: ضيف نط مزدوج للقطة بتاعتك في اللعبة.
steps: A double jump lets characters leap a second time while floating mid-air, opening up new platforming heights and exploration routes in your game worlds.
For example, if your cat is already falling after its first jump, pressing the spacebar again triggers a quick upward boost instead of doing nothing.
This works by tracking jump counts using a numeric variable that decreases each time you trigger a mid-air jump action.
A second example is rocket boots in a sci-fi game that give players extra lift only after collecting a special battery power-up item.
Rule of thumb: always reset your air jump counter back to maximum right when your sprite touches the ground platform.
Game developers use double jumps heavily in platformers like Mario and Sonic to make navigating tricky gaps much more fluid and fun.
lessons.example: To make a double jump, create a variable called 'jumps'. When touching the floor, set 'jumps' to 2. When pressing the space key and 'jumps' > 0, change y by 12 and change 'jumps' by -1. This lets the sprite jump once from the ground and once more while flying through the air!
lessons.mistake: Forgetting to reset the jump counter when touching the ground, which means you can never jump again. Fix this by adding a 'set jumps to 2' block inside your floor collision checker.
lessons.recap: Double jumps use a counter variable to let players leap again in mid-air. Always reset the counter when landing on solid ground.

q.t: What variable helps us track how many jumps are left?
q.why: We track remaining jumps using a specific jump count variable.

q.t: When should you reset your jump counter?
q.why: Resetting when touching the floor lets you jump again normally.

q.t: What happens to the jump counter during a mid-air jump?
q.why: We subtract one from the counter each time a mid-air jump is used.

lessons.sub: variable jump height; hold to jump higher; physics feel
teaching: Control jump height by how long you hold the jump key.
Apply weaker upward speed while the jump key is actively held down.
Test different jump force values to find the smoothest arcade feel.
Always combine this with standard gravity falling blocks.
lessons.explainAr: هتعلم إزاي نخلي نطّة الشخصية أعلى لو ضغطنا مطولاً على الزرار. ده بيخلي اللعبة تحسها زي الألعاب الحقيقية.
lessons.exampleEn: If the jump key is held, apply extra upward velocity for a higher leap.
lessons.exampleAr: لو زرار النط مضغوط، بندفع الشخصية لفوق أكتر عشان تنط أعلى.
lessons.practiceEn: Make your jump height depend on holding the spacebar.
lessons.practiceAr: خلي ارتفاع النطة يعتمد على الضغط المستمر على مسافة.
steps: Variable gravity jump lets players control how high they leap based on how long they hold down the jump key.
For instance, tapping the key gives a tiny hop over a small obstacle, while holding it down reaches a high ledge.
This works by checking if the jump key is still pressed during the upward movement loop, adding extra upward speed step-by-step.
Another example is a superhero character who floats higher into the clouds the longer you hold the power button.
Rule of thumb: keep the initial tap quick and snappy, then add gentle extra lift only while the key remains down.
Game designers use variable jump heights to give players precise control over movement puzzles and platform timing.
lessons.example: Set y-velocity to 15. Then repeat 8 times: if key space pressed, change y by 4 and reduce y-velocity. This makes short taps low jumps and long holds high jumps!
lessons.mistake: Applying constant high upward force without checking key status, which causes the character to float away uncontrollably. Fix this by checking key presses inside a short repeat loop.
lessons.recap: Variable jump height gives players precise control by checking if jump keys are held down. It creates professional, responsive arcade physics.

q.t: What does a variable jump height depend on?
o: How long you hold the key
q.why: Holding the key longer adds extra upward lift.

q.t: How does a quick tap affect the jump?
q.why: Tapping quickly stops the extra upward boost early.

q.t: What makes variable jumping feel good?
q.why: Responsive physics mimic real platformer games.

lessons.sub: wall touch; slow fall; sliding down walls; physics tweak
teaching: Detect when your player sprite touches a side wall.
Slow down your falling speed while sliding against the wall.
Combine wall touch sensing with keyboard arrow controls.
Always test wall friction so sliding feels natural and smooth.
lessons.explainAr: هتعلم إزاي نخلي الشخصية تتزحلق ببطء وهي نازلة على الحيطة. ده بيخلينا نعمل ألعاب أكشن ومغامرات احترافية.
lessons.exampleEn: If touching a wall and falling, reduce gravity effect to slide slowly.
lessons.exampleAr: لو بنلمس حيطة وواقعين لتحت، بنقلل سرعة السقوط عشان نتزحلق ببطء.
lessons.practiceEn: Add a slow slide effect when touching side walls.
lessons.practiceAr: ضيف تأثير انزلاق بطيء عند ملامسة الحوائط الجانبية.
steps: Wall sliding physics allows characters to slide down vertical walls slowly instead of dropping like a stone.
For example, your ninja cat can press against a vertical cliff face and descend gracefully to a lower platform.
This is coded by checking if you are touching a wall color while falling downward, then reducing your negative y-speed.
Another example is a climbing robot that grips smooth glass surfaces to slow its descent.
Rule of thumb: use a small negative speed value like -1 or -2 during wall contact to create a realistic sliding friction feel.
Platformer games use wall sliding to add vertical depth, acrobatic moves, and complex maze navigation.
lessons.example: If touching wall color and y-velocity < 0, set y-velocity to -2. This makes the sprite glide smoothly down the side of the obstacle instead of plunging straight down.
lessons.mistake: Glued completely to the wall without falling at all. Fix this by allowing a small negative sliding speed so gravity still pulls you downward gently.
lessons.recap: Wall sliding slows down downward speed when touching side walls. It creates acrobatic movement mechanics for platform games.

q.t: What happens to falling speed during a wall slide?
q.why: Wall sliding reduces falling speed to simulate friction.

q.t: What do you need to sense for wall sliding?

q.t: Why use wall sliding in games?
q.why: It adds fun acrobatic movement and navigation options.

lessons.sub: wall kick; pushing away from walls; horizontal leap
teaching: Combine wall sliding with a sideways push when jumping.
Apply horizontal velocity away from the wall you touch.
Check which side of the wall you are on to push correctly.
Always make sure you can only wall jump while sliding.
lessons.explainAr: هتعلم إزاي نقفز بعيد عن الحيطة واحنا متزحلقين عليها. الحركة دي بتخلينا نطلع بين حيطين ضيقين.
lessons.exampleEn: When touching a wall and pressing jump, push up and away horizontally.
lessons.exampleAr: لما نلمس حيطة ونضغط نط، بنتحرك لفوق ولبره بعيد عن الحيطة.
lessons.practiceEn: Make your character jump off walls to climb higher.
lessons.practiceAr: خلي شخصيتك تقفز من الحوائط عشان تطلع لفوق.
steps: Wall jumping lets characters kick off vertical walls to leap upward and across narrow gaps.
For example, your ninja can bounce back and forth between two close vertical walls to reach the top of a tower.
This works by checking if you are touching a wall and pressing the jump key, then instantly adding both upward and sideways speeds away from the wall.
Another example is a parkour runner pushing off brick walls to cross city rooftops.
Rule of thumb: push the player in the opposite direction of the wall they are touching so they leap outward correctly.
Game designers use wall jumping to build intricate vertical puzzle rooms and rewarding movement challenges.
lessons.example: If touching left wall and space pressed, set y-velocity to 12 and x-velocity to 8. The sprite kicks off the wall and shoots up and right!
lessons.mistake: Jumping straight up into the same wall instead of away from it. Fix this by adding a positive or negative x-velocity push opposite to the wall's side.
lessons.recap: Wall jumping combines wall touch detection with an outward horizontal push and upward leap. It lets players scale vertical shafts.

q.t: Which directions do you move during a wall jump?
o: Up and away from the wall
q.why: Wall jumping gives both upward lift and a sideways push.

q.t: What triggers a wall jump?
o: Pressing jump while touching a wall
q.why: You must touch the wall and press the jump key.

q.t: Why do we push in the opposite direction?
o: To leap away from the wall
q.why: Pushing the opposite way ensures you jump outward.

lessons.sub: riding platforms; syncing player x y; moving obstacles
teaching: Make platform sprites glide back and forth across the screen.
Detect when your player stands directly on top of the moving platform.
Carry the player along with the platform's exact movement.
Always test that walking off the platform restores normal gravity.
lessons.explainAr: هتعلم إزاي نخلي الشخصية تقف وتتحرك مع المنصات المتحركة. ده بيخلي اللعبة فيها تحديات حركة ذكية.
lessons.exampleEn: When standing on the moving platform, change player x by platform speed.
lessons.exampleAr: لما نقف على المنصة المتحركة، بنحرك الشخصية بنفس سرعة المنصة.
lessons.practiceEn: Make your player ride horizontally moving platforms.
lessons.practiceAr: خلي شخصيتك ترتكز وتتحرك مع المنصات الأفقية.
steps: Moving platform physics lets characters ride floating blocks that glide back and forth across empty chasms.
For instance, your cat can hop onto a floating cloud elevator and ride it safely across a river of lava.
This is coded by checking if the player is touching the platform from above, then adding the platform's step movement directly to the player's coordinates.
Another example is a spaceship elevator lifting miners up to higher cavern levels.
Rule of thumb: update player position by the platform's exact speed amount every frame the player stands on top.
Game designers use moving platforms to test player timing, positioning, and navigation skills.
lessons.example: If touching platform and standing on top, change player x by platform_speed. The player glides along with the platform without sliding off!
lessons.mistake: The player stands on the platform but stays behind as it moves away. Fix this by adding the platform's speed value to the player's x position.
lessons.recap: Moving platforms carry standing players by adding platform movement to player coordinates. They add dynamic transit puzzles to levels.

q.t: What happens when you stand on a moving platform?
q.why: Standing on it carries you along with its movement.

q.t: How do you make the player move with the platform?
o: Add platform speed to player position
q.why: Adding the platform speed syncs player position.

q.t: What should happen when you walk off the platform?
q.why: Leaving the platform restores normal gravity and falling.

act.goal: Find the line where the player fails to move with the platform.
lines: If touching platform, change player x by 0
If not touching platform, apply gravity
act.fix: If touching platform, change player x by platform_speed
act.success: The player successfully rode the moving platform across the gap!

lessons.sub: super bounce; bounce pad; high velocity launch; elastic force
teaching: Create a trampoline or spring sprite on the ground.
Detect when your player lands on top of the trampoline.
Apply a huge upward velocity boost to launch the player high.
Always use sound effects to make the bounce feel satisfying.
lessons.explainAr: هتعلم إزاي نعمل ترامبولين بيقذف الشخصية لفوق بسرعة كبيرة. ده بيخلي اللعبة مليانة حركات بهلوانية سريعة.
lessons.exampleEn: When touching the trampoline, set upward jump speed to a very high number.
lessons.exampleAr: لما نلمس الترامبولين، بنخلي سرعة النط لفوق رقم كبير جداً.
lessons.practiceEn: Add a bouncy spring pad that launches your player sky-high.
lessons.practiceAr: ضيف ترامبولين بيقذف شخصيتك لعالي السحابة.
steps: Bouncy trampoline physics simulates elastic springs that launch characters high into the air with great force.
For example, your cat can land on a green trampoline pad and shoot straight up to the top of the screen.
This works by checking collision with the trampoline sprite, then instantly setting the player's upward velocity to an extra high value like 25.
Another example is a pinball bumper that blasts the silver ball across the entire game board.
Rule of thumb: use a high initial velocity boost combined with a satisfying sound effect to maximize player feedback.
Game designers use trampolines to create fast shortcuts, secret high areas, and energetic gameplay pacing.
lessons.example: If touching trampoline, set y-velocity to 22 and play sound 'boing'. The sprite shoots sky-high with an exciting bounce effect!
lessons.mistake: Setting the bounce speed too low so the player barely leaves the pad. Fix this by using a high upward velocity number like 20 or 25.
lessons.recap: Trampolines detect player collision and apply a large upward velocity boost. They create fun, high-flying vertical shortcuts.

q.t: What does a trampoline do when touched?
q.why: It applies a large upward velocity boost.

q.t: How do we code the bounce strength?
o: Set y-velocity to a high number
q.why: A high y-velocity value creates the powerful launch.

q.t: What adds great feedback to a trampoline bounce?
q.why: Sound effects make bounces feel satisfying and alive.

act.title: Trampoline Launch Test
act.goal: Predict what happens when touching the trampoline.
options: The sprite bounces super high into the air
The sprite teleports to the left
act.success: The trampoline launched the character high into the sky!

lessons.sub: momentum; sliding friction; ice surface; slippery movement
teaching: Create an ice floor zone with low friction.
Keep moving slightly after releasing the arrow keys on ice.
Gradually slow down momentum instead of stopping instantly.
Always test ice movement so turning feels challenging and fun.
lessons.explainAr: هتعلم إزاي نعمل أرضية جليد الزلاجة. الشخصية بتكمل مشي شوية بعد ما نسيب زرار الحركة عشان مفيش احتكاك.
lessons.exampleEn: On ice, glide smoothly by letting speed reduce slowly instead of stopping at once.
lessons.exampleAr: على الجليد، بنتحرك بانسيابية عن طريق تقليل السرعة بالتدريج.
lessons.practiceEn: Make movement slippery when walking across ice blocks.
lessons.practiceAr: خلي الحركة زلقة لما نمشي على بلوكات الجليد.
steps: Slippery ice physics simulates low friction surfaces where characters slide and glide before coming to a stop.
For example, your penguin can skate across an frozen lake, sliding past items if you don't brake early.
This works by multiplying your movement speed by a decimal like 0.9 each frame instead of setting speed straight to zero when keys are released.
Another example is a race car driving over an oil slick on the track.
Rule of thumb: use momentum math so stopping takes time, creating a fun sliding challenge for the player.
Game designers use ice physics to add variety, challenge precision timing, and test player control skills.
lessons.example: If on ice, change x-velocity by key press, then set x-velocity to x-velocity * 0.92. The sprite slides gracefully across the icy ground!
lessons.mistake: Stopping instantly on ice just like regular ground. Fix this by using momentum multiplication instead of resetting speed to zero immediately.
lessons.recap: Ice physics uses momentum multiplication to create low friction sliding movement. It adds fun steering challenges to levels.

q.t: What makes ice physics feel different from normal ground?
q.why: Low friction causes sliding momentum after releasing keys.

q.t: How do we code gradual slowing on ice?
o: Multiply speed by a decimal like 0.9
q.why: Multiplying by a decimal gradually reduces speed.

q.t: Why add ice physics to a game?
o: To make it impossible to win
q.why: It adds variety and tests player control.

act.goal: Arrange the blocks for slippery ice movement.

act.success: The character glided smoothly across the slippery ice!

lessons.sub: drop through platforms; phase down; downward pass
teaching: Design thin floating platforms you can jump up through.
Allow players to drop straight down by pressing down arrow and jump.
Temporarily ignore platform collisions when dropping through.
Always restore normal landing after passing through the platform.
lessons.explainAr: هتعلم إزاي نقفز من تحت المنصة ونطلع فوقها، وبرضو نقدر ننزل لتحت لو ضغطنا زرار السهم لتحت.
lessons.exampleEn: If pressing down arrow while on a platform, move down slightly so you fall through.
lessons.exampleAr: لو ضغطنا سهم لتحت واحنا على المنصة، بننزل تحتها عشان نعدي.
lessons.practiceEn: Allow your player to drop down through thin floating platforms.
lessons.practiceAr: خلي شخصيتك تقدر تنزل لتحت عبر المنصات الرفيعة.
steps: One-way platform drop allows characters to jump up through thin floating floors from below, but stand on top of them normally.
For instance, your cat can leap up to higher levels in a tower, then press down arrow to drop back down quickly.
This works by checking if the player is pressing the down key while standing on the platform, then nudging their y-position downward so they clear the solid top edge.
Another example is multi-tier shelving in a grocery store puzzle game.
Rule of thumb: make platforms thin sensors so standing detection only triggers when falling from above.
Game developers use one-way platforms to make multi-level vertical map layouts clean and easy to navigate.
lessons.example: If touching platform and key down arrow pressed, change y by -5. The player drops straight through the thin platform floor!
lessons.mistake: Falling through platforms even when jumping onto them from above. Fix this by checking that your falling speed is downward before triggering the collision stop.
lessons.recap: One-way platforms let players jump up through them and drop down by pressing down arrow. They create versatile vertical layouts.

q.t: What is special about a one-way platform?
o: You can jump up through it
q.why: You can pass through it from below and stand on top.

q.t: How do you drop down through a one-way platform?
o: Press down arrow and move down
q.why: Pressing down arrow moves you past the solid surface.

q.t: Why use one-way platforms in games?
q.why: They make multi-level vertical navigation smooth.

act.goal: Match platform controls to their results.
act.success: The player dropped through the one-way platform smoothly!

lessons.sub: edge teleport; left to right wrap; infinite screen bounds
teaching: Detect when your player walks off the left edge of the screen.
Instantly teleport the player to the right edge of the screen.
Do the same for left-to-right and top-to-bottom boundaries.
Always test screen wrapping so characters never get stuck off-screen.
lessons.explainAr: هتعلم إزاي نخلي الشخصية لما تطلع من شمال الشاشة تظهر تاني من اليمين. الحركة دي بتعمل عوالم دائرية.
lessons.exampleEn: If x position is less than -240, set x position to 240.
lessons.exampleAr: لو موضع س أقل من -240، بننقل الموضع لـ 240 الناحية التانية.
lessons.practiceEn: Make your sprite wrap around from one side of the screen to the other.
lessons.practiceAr: خلي الشخصية تظهر الناحية التانية لما تخرج من حافة الشاشة.
steps: Screen wrap-around lets characters exiting one side of the screen instantly reappear on the opposite side.
For example, your spaceship flying off the right edge of the display pops out safely on the left side.
This works by checking coordinate bounds, like if x > 240, setting x to -240.
Another example is classic arcade games where pellets and player ships loop continuously across boundaries.
Rule of thumb: match your wrap boundary numbers to the exact edge coordinates of the Scratch stage (-240 and 240).
Game designers use screen wrap-around to create continuous, infinite-feeling playing fields without scrolling.
lessons.example: If x position > 240, set x to -240. The sprite exits the right side of the stage and seamlessly appears on the left side!
lessons.mistake: Teleporting right back and forth in an infinite glitch loop. Fix this by placing the teleport threshold just outside the visible screen edges.
lessons.recap: Screen wrap-around teleports sprites to the opposite side when crossing stage boundaries. It creates infinite looping game worlds.

q.t: What happens when a sprite crosses the right edge with screen wrap?
o: It reappears on the left side
q.why: It teleports to the opposite side of the screen.

q.t: What are the standard x edge limits on the Scratch stage?
q.why: The Scratch stage width boundaries are -240 and 240.

q.t: Why use screen wrap-around in a game?
q.why: It creates continuous looping playing fields.

act.title: Screen Wrap Bug
act.goal: Find the wrong coordinate limit in the wrap script.
lines: If x position > 500, set x to -240
If x position < -240, set x to 240
act.fix: If x position > 240, set x to -240
act.success: The screen wrap-around teleported the sprite perfectly across the stage!

lessons.sub: term integration; gravity; jump; platforms; boss battle
teaching: Combine gravity, jumping, platforms, and health into one grand boss game.
Program a boss sprite that moves and shoots projectiles across the arena.
Code win and loss states using score and health variables.
Test your complete arcade game from start to finish.
lessons.explainAr: هنجمع كل اللي تعلمناه من جاذبية، ونط، ومنصات، وصحة في لعبة معركة زعيم نهائية وممتعة.
lessons.exampleEn: Combine gravity movement, platforms, and boss health into a complete arcade game.
lessons.exampleAr: اجمع حركة الجاذبية، والمنصات، وصحة الزعيم في لعبة آركيد متكاملة.
lessons.practiceEn: Build and test the final arcade physics boss battle game.
lessons.practiceAr: ابني واختبر لعبة معركة الزعيم النهائية بفيزياء الآركيد.
steps: Arcade physics boss arena is the ultimate capstone project integrating all physics mechanics learned this term into one game.
For instance, your cat must jump across moving platforms, avoid slippery ice, and double jump to dodge boss laser attacks.
This works by combining gravity loops, platform collisions, health variables, and enemy AI into a structured script.
Another example is fighting a floating robot boss while riding trampolines and dodging falling spikes.
Rule of thumb: build your game piece by piece—test movement first, then platforms, then add the boss and health last.
Game developers combine all mechanics together to create rich, polished, and unforgettable boss battle experiences.
lessons.example: If player touches boss attack, reduce health by 1. If boss health reaches 0, broadcast 'win'! This creates a complete, exciting arcade boss challenge.
lessons.mistake: Putting all blocks in one gigantic unreadable script. Fix this by using separate 'My Blocks' and event broadcasts for movement, boss AI, and health.
lessons.recap: The boss arena project combines gravity, platforms, movement physics, and health into a complete game. It celebrates all your game design skills!

q.t: What does the capstone boss arena combine?
o: All physics mechanics and health systems
q.why: It integrates gravity, jumping, platforms, and health.

q.t: What is the best way to build a big game project?
o: Piece by piece and test as you go
q.why: Building step-by-step ensures each part works properly.

q.t: What happens when boss health reaches zero?
q.why: Reaching zero boss health triggers the win state.

items: Set up player gravity and movement controls

teaching: Special symbols like copyright or greater-than need special codes called entities.
Use © to display the copyright symbol © on your webpage.

lessons.sub: strong; em; mark; small; inline
teaching: Inline tags let you style specific words right inside a paragraph.

Try highlighting an exciting word using the <mark> tag.

lessons.sub: ::before; ::after; ::first-letter; content property
teaching: Pseudo-elements let you style specific parts of an element, like its very first letter.
p::first-letter { font-size: 2em; } makes the opening letter huge and bold.
Add a cute star before every heading using the content property.
Remember to use two colons (::) for pseudo-elements to separate them from classes.
lessons.explainAr: العناصر الوهمية بتخلينا نتحكم في أجزاء معينة من النص زي أول حرف أو نضيف ديكور قبل العنصر. دي أداة سحرية لتزيين الصفحات.
lessons.exampleEn: h1::after { content: ' ★'; }
lessons.exampleAr: h1::after { content: ' ★'; }
lessons.practiceEn: Style the first letter of a paragraph to be red.
lessons.practiceAr: اجعل لون أول حرف في الفقرة لونه أحمر.
lessons.ar: العناصر الوهمية في سي إس إس

lessons.sub: custom properties; root selector; var() function
teaching: CSS variables store custom values like brand colors so you can reuse them easily.
:root { --main-color: blue; } defines a global variable for the whole page.
Use color: var(--main-color); to apply your variable to a heading element.
Always start your custom variable name with two dashes (--).
lessons.explainAr: متغيرات سي إس إس بتسمح لنا نحفظ الألوان أو المقاسات في مكان واحد ونستخدمها في كل حتة. لو حبينا نغير لون الموقع كله بنغير سطر واحد بس!
lessons.exampleEn: :root { --theme: purple; } h2 { color: var(--theme); }
lessons.exampleAr: :root { --theme: purple; } h2 { color: var(--theme); }
lessons.practiceEn: Create a root variable for background color and apply it.
lessons.practiceAr: اصنع متغير لصفر الخلفية في الجذر وطبقه على الصفحة.

lessons.titleAr: ظلال الصناديق في سي إس إس
lessons.sub: box-shadow offsets; blur radius; spread; color
teaching: Box shadows add depth and 3D realism to flat boxes and cards on your screen.
box-shadow: 10px 10px 5px gray; adds horizontal, vertical, and blur effects.
Apply a soft shadow to an image card to make it pop out.
The first value moves the shadow right, and the second moves it down.
lessons.explainAr: ظلال الصناديق بتخلي العناصر تحس كأنها طايرة فوق الصفحة زي الكروت البارزة. القيم بتحدد اتجاه الظل ومقدار ضبابيته.
lessons.exampleEn: div { box-shadow: 0 4px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.2); }
lessons.exampleAr: div { box-shadow: 0 4px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.2); }
lessons.practiceEn: Add a subtle shadow to a profile card element.
lessons.practiceAr: أضف ظل خفيف ولطيف لصندوق بطاقة الملف الشخصي.
lessons.ar: ظلال الصناديق في سي إس إس

lessons.titleAr: ظلال النصوص في سي إس إس
lessons.sub: text-shadow offsets; blur; color; glowing effects
teaching: Text shadows make your headings stand out with cool lighting effects.
text-shadow: 2px 2px 4px black; creates a neat shadow behind your letters.
Make a title look like it is glowing with neon colors.
Keep blur values small so the text remains easy and clear to read.
lessons.explainAr: ظلال النصوص بتدي تأثيرات بصرية مذهلة للعناوين وتخليها تلمع أو تبرز بوضوح. لازم نخلي الظل هادئ عشان الكتابة تفضل مقروءة.
lessons.exampleEn: h1 { text-shadow: 3px 3px 5px red; }
lessons.exampleAr: h1 { text-shadow: 3px 3px 5px red; }
lessons.practiceEn: Give your main heading a blue text shadow.
lessons.practiceAr: اعمل ظل أزرق للنص الرئيسي في العنوان.
lessons.ar: ظلال النصوص في سي إس إس

lessons.titleAr: الزوايا الدائرية في سي إس إس
lessons.sub: border-radius; circular images; pill buttons
teaching: Border radius bends sharp box corners into smooth, modern curved edges.
border-radius: 10px; gently rounds the four corners of any box.
Turn a square profile picture into a perfect circle using 50%.
Use high pixel values or 50% to make pill-shaped buttons easily.
lessons.explainAr: خاصية تدوير الحدود بتخلي الحواف الحادة ناعمة وجميلة زي الأزرار الحديثة والصور الدائرية. نسبة 50% تحول المربع لدائرة كاملة.
lessons.exampleEn: img { border-radius: 50%; }
lessons.exampleAr: img { border-radius: 50%; }
lessons.practiceEn: Round the corners of a photo box by 15 pixels.
lessons.practiceAr: اجعل زوايا صندوق الصورة دائرية بمقدار 15 بكسل.
lessons.ar: الزوايا الدائرية في سي إس إس

lessons.titleAr: فلاتر الصور في سي إس إس
lessons.sub: grayscale; blur; brightness; contrast effects
teaching: CSS filters change the look of images directly in the browser like photo apps.
filter: grayscale(100%); turns any full-color photo into black and white.
Blur an image background slightly using the blur() filter function.
Combine multiple filters together by writing them in one line with spaces.
lessons.explainAr: فلاتر الصور بتعدل شكل الصور مباشرة في المتصفح من غير برامج تعديل. نقدر نعملها أبيض وأسود أو نغوشها بسهولة.
lessons.exampleEn: img { filter: brightness(150%); }
lessons.exampleAr: img { filter: brightness(150%); }
lessons.practiceEn: Apply a grayscale filter to all website product photos.
lessons.practiceAr: طبق فلاتر الأبيض والأسود على صور المنتجات في الموقع.
lessons.ar: فلاتر الصور في سي إس إس

lessons.titleAr: الانتقالات السلسة في سي إس إس
lessons.sub: transition-property; duration; timing-function; delay
teaching: Transitions make style changes animate smoothly instead of jumping instantly.
transition: all 0.5s ease; makes property shifts take half a second.
Animate a button growing larger smoothly when the mouse hovers over it.
Always state the duration in seconds (s) or milliseconds (ms).
lessons.explainAr: الانتقالات بتخلي التغيرات في الشكل تحصل بهدوء وناعم بدل ما تنط فجأة. دي بتخلي الموقع يبמו احترافي ومريح للعين.
lessons.exampleEn: button { transition: background 0.3s; }
lessons.exampleAr: button { transition: background 0.3s; }
lessons.practiceEn: Add a smooth one-second transition to a box width.
lessons.practiceAr: أضف انتقالا سلسا مدته ثانية واحدة لعرض الصندوق.
lessons.ar: الانتقالات السلسة في سي إس إس

lessons.titleAr: التحويلات ثنائية الأبعاد في سي إس إس
lessons.sub: rotate; scale; translate; skew effects
teaching: 2D transforms let you move, spin, stretch, or tilt elements on a flat page.
transform: rotate(45deg); tilts your box diagonally like a diamond shape.
Make an icon grow bigger when hovered using transform: scale(1.2);
Transforms work great together with smooth CSS transitions for animations.
lessons.explainAr: التحويلات ثنائية الأبعاد بتخلينا نلف العناصر أو نكبرهم أو نحركهم من مكانهم. دي بتدي حركة ممتعة وتفاعلية لموقعك.
lessons.exampleEn: div { transform: scale(1.1); }
lessons.exampleAr: div { transform: scale(1.1); }
lessons.practiceEn: Rotate an image card by 10 degrees.
lessons.practiceAr: قم بتدوير بطاقة الصورة بزاوية 10 درجات.
lessons.ar: التحويلات ثنائية الأبعاد في سي إس إس

lessons.sub: variables; shadows; filters; hover effects integration
teaching: Combine all your advanced CSS styling tricks into one gorgeous web portfolio.
Use CSS root variables for colors, rounded corners for cards, and box shadows.
Add cool hover states and 2D transforms to make your project interactive.
Review your code carefully to ensure everything looks polished and neat.
lessons.explainAr: في الدرس ده هنجمع كل المهارات اللي اتعلمناها زي الظلال، المتغيرات، والفلاتر عشان نصمم معرض أعمال فخم وجميل. ده مشروعنا الختامي للترم!
lessons.exampleEn: :root { --brand: blue; } .card { border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: 0 4px 10px gray; }
lessons.exampleAr: :root { --brand: blue; } .card { border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: 0 4px 10px gray; }
lessons.practiceEn: Style a complete portfolio card using variables, shadows, and hover.
lessons.practiceAr: صمم بطاقة معرض أعمال كاملة باستخدام المتغيرات والظلال وحالة الهوفر.

lessons.sub: push; pop; modifying arrays; dynamic lists
teaching: An array method is a built-in tool that helps us change or inspect our list easily.
Using push() adds a new item to the very end of your JavaScript array.
Try adding a new score to your gaming high scores list using the push method.
Remember that push changes the original array directly, so watch out for unexpected modifications.
lessons.explainAr: طرق المصفوفات هي أدوات جاهزة تساعدنا نضيف عناصر جديدة أو نشيلها بسهولة. الـ push بتزود عنصر في الآخر، والـ pop بتشيله.
lessons.exampleEn: let scores = [10, 20]; scores.push(30); results in [10, 20, 30] because push adds to the end.
lessons.exampleAr: لما نكتب scores.push(30)، المصفوفة بتكبر ويبقى فيها رقم 30 في الآخر.
lessons.practiceEn: Add a new fruit to your shopping list array using the push method.
lessons.practiceAr: ضيف فاكهة جديدة لمصفوفة المشتريات بتاعتك باستخدام طريقة push.
steps: An array can grow or shrink while your webpage runs using special built-in JavaScript methods.
We use players.push('Ali') to safely insert a new participant right at the end of the list.
The push method automatically updates the array length and places the item in the next available index.
Conversely, players.pop() removes the final item from the array and returns it for us to use.
Always remember that push and pop directly change your original array, so use them carefully.
Real-life use: Managing a shopping cart list where users can continuously add or remove items.
lessons.mistake: Forgetting that pop removes the item and alters the array length at the same time.
lessons.recap: Array methods like push and pop let us dynamically add and remove items from our lists. They keep our data organized as user actions change the webpage.

q.t: What does push() do to an array?
o: Adds an item to the end
q.why: The push method adds new elements to the very end of an array.

q.t: Which method removes the last item?
q.why: The pop method removes the final element from an array.

q.t: Where are items placed when using push?
q.why: Push always adds items to the end of the array.

lessons.titleAr: تعديل أول المصفوفة: shift و unshift
lessons.sub: shift; unshift; beginning of array; queue management
teaching: Sometimes we need to add or remove items from the very beginning of an array.
Using unshift() adds a brand new element to index zero, shifting others forward.
Try adding a VIP guest to the front of your event queue using unshift.
Remember that changing the start of a large array takes a bit more computer effort.
lessons.explainAr: الـ unshift بتضيف عنصر في أول المصفوفة، والـ shift بتشيل أول عنصر. دي مفيدة جداً لما نحب نرتب طابور انتظار.
lessons.exampleEn: let queue = ['Bob']; queue.unshift('Ana'); results in ['Ana', 'Bob'] because unshift adds to the front.
lessons.exampleAr: لما نستخدم unshift، العنصر الجديد بيدخل في الأول خالص.
lessons.practiceEn: Remove the first customer from your waiting list using the shift method.
lessons.practiceAr: شيل أول زبون من طابور الانتظار باستخدام طريقة shift.
steps: Manipulating the front of an array requires methods that handle the very first index position.
We use queue.unshift('Sara') to place a new item at index zero, pushing everything else down.
The unshift method returns the new total length of the modified array after insertion.
On the other hand, queue.shift() removes the first element and shifts all remaining items left.
Always keep track of index shifts so you do not accidentally lose track of your data elements.
Real-life use: Managing a ticket line where the first person in line gets served and leaves first.
lessons.mistake: Confusing unshift (adds to front) with push (adds to back).
lessons.recap: Shift and unshift let you manage the start of an array easily. They are perfect for handling queues and waiting lists in your apps.

q.t: What does unshift() do?
q.why: Unshift inserts elements at the very beginning of an array.

q.t: What does shift() return?
q.why: Shift removes and returns the first element of the array.

q.t: Which method adds an item at index 0?
q.why: Unshift places the new item at the start of the array.

lessons.sub: indexOf; finding position; searching arrays; minus one
teaching: indexOf lets us search inside an array to find where a specific item lives.
If the item exists, JavaScript returns its exact index number, like 2 or 5.
Try searching your friend list to see if 'Mona' is included and where she stands.
If the item is missing entirely, indexOf safely returns minus one (-1).
lessons.explainAr: طريقة indexOf بتدور جوه المصفوفة وترجع لنا مكان العنصر فين بالضبط. لو العنصر مش موجود، بترجع رقم سالب واحد (-1).
lessons.exampleEn: let fruits = ['apple', 'banana']; fruits.indexOf('banana'); returns 1 because banana is at index 1.
lessons.exampleAr: لما ندور على banana، الكود بيرجع رقم 1 لأنها في الترتيب الثاني.
lessons.practiceEn: Find the index of 'blue' in your colors array using indexOf.
lessons.practiceAr: دور على مكان لون 'blue' في مصفوفة الألوان بتاعتك باستخدام indexOf.
steps: Searching manually through a large array of data is tedious, so JavaScript provides indexOf.
We write colors.indexOf('red') to ask JavaScript to scan the array and locate 'red'.
If found, it hands back the exact index number where that item is stored in memory.
If the search fails, indexOf returns -1, which is a helpful signal for conditional checks.
Always remember that indexOf is case-sensitive, so 'Red' and 'red' are treated differently.
Real-life use: Checking if a user's chosen username already exists in a registered list.
lessons.mistake: Forgetting that indexOf returns -1 when an item is not found, leading to bugs in if statements.
lessons.recap: indexOf is a fast way to locate items inside arrays. It returns the index number or -1 if the search item is absent.

q.t: What does indexOf return if an item is missing?
q.why: A return value of -1 specifically means the item was not found.

q.t: Is indexOf case-sensitive?
q.why: Yes, 'Apple' and 'apple' are different strings to indexOf.

q.t: What does indexOf return when a match is found?
q.why: It returns the numerical index of the matching element.
